purpose: Repair round: turn the Round-6 diagnosis into a controlled A/B on ONE tree (same solver, same closure, same grid), so that (a) the drive-width defect is shown to be detectable by the metric, (b) the fix is shown to remove it, (c) the velocity diagnostic is shown to report the physical velocity. Round 6 compared a pre-fix snapshot with a post-fix snapshot across two worktrees; that is a two-tree comparison and cannot exclude tree drift. This round varies only the driving normalisation inside a single process.

design.controlled: solver (GPUCorePathSolver, FP64FP64, eager), tau=1.1 (nu=0.2), nx=8, nz=4, init=rest, declared u_max_target=0.05, steady tolerance 1e-12, check every 200 steps
design.changed: only the body-force normalisation: closure_width derives a = 8 nu u_max / H_wall^2 with H_wall = ny-1 for nebb and ny-2 for halfway; legacy_halfway_width derives a = 8 nu u_max / (ny-2)^2 regardless of closure (= the pre-fix formula, emulated exactly by u_max_target *= (H_wall/(ny-2))^2 on the fixed tree)
design.unit_of_analysis: one steady channel solution per cell of the 2x2x2 design
design.repetitions: deterministic solver, no stochastic terms (float64, fixed seed irrelevant); each cell run once, the analytic parabola is evaluated in closed form at the same y nodes
design.confounders: two-tree drift (removed by the single-process design), convergence level (recorded as steps_used + steady_residual per arm), nz/nx wall-periodicity (identical across arms)

predeclared_checks.claim: With the fixed normalisation the achieved centre-line velocity equals the declared target on BOTH closures.
predeclared_checks.pass_if: |ratio_vs_declared - 1| < 0.01 for wall_bc in {nebb, halfway}, ny in {10, 18}
predeclared_checks.falsified_if: |ratio_vs_declared - 1| >= 0.01 at any cell -> the fix does not deliver the declared velocity

predeclared_checks.claim: The same metric recovers the pre-fix overshoot when the drive is normalised with the legacy half-way width.
predeclared_checks.falsified_if: ratio_vs_declared stays within 1 % of 1 -> the metric cannot see the defect and P1 proves nothing

predeclared_checks.claim: On the half-way closure the two normalisations must coincide (H_wall == ny-2), i.e. the legacy width is only wrong for a wall-node closure.
predeclared_checks.falsified_if: >= 1e-9 -> the emulation is not exactly the legacy formula, so P2 would be confounded

predeclared_checks.claim: (holdych1998 exactness) Once the drive and the momentum definition are consistent, the plane-Poiseuille steady state of this BGK+Guo lattice is exactly quadratic, so the physical-velocity error against the closed-form parabola is round-off at every ny.
predeclared_checks.falsified_if: >= 1e-8 at any cell -> genuine truncation error remains; report the measured profile error, no tuning

predeclared_checks.claim: The public velocity diagnostic reports the physical velocity (raw moment + a/2), not the raw moment.
predeclared_checks.pass_if: in [0.99, 1.01] on the closure_width arm for both closures
predeclared_checks.falsified_if: < 0.05 -> the diagnostic still reports the raw moment (Round-5 behaviour)

error_judgement_rule: Owner standard: pointwise error against the analytic reference > 15 % unacceptable, ecosystem stretch < 3 %. Every number quoted in REPORT_R7.md must be produced by run_xval_r7_drive_width_ab.py and stored in artifacts/r7/.
no_tuning_rule: No tolerance, grid, viscosity, or step count may be changed after seeing a result. Any post-hoc hypothesis is added as a new id with its own JSON entry and its own run.
